# User preferences (keywords: preference, version numbers, dependencies, formatting)

- Always include version numbers when discussing software dependencies or libraries (Apr 5 2024 instruction).
- Earlier preference (Mar 15 2024): syntax-highlighted fenced code blocks with a language tag.

Open item from the Apr 5 2024 full-project answer: the pins in requirements.txt (Werkzeug 2.3.8, SQLAlchemy 2.0.25,
Flask-Caching 2.0.2, gunicorn 21.2.0, pytest 8.0.2, pytest-cov 4.1.0, black 24.2.0, Jinja2 3.1.3) were written from memory
and not verified against PyPI. The answer told the user to run `pip install --dry-run` to check them.

## Apr 25 2024 session: "pragmatic security, no UX or responsiveness cost" request
- User cited "my 25th preference statement". No such numbered list exists in memory; only the two preferences above are stored.
  Asked user to restate it. Do not invent its content.
- Applied the two stored preferences: version numbers on all dependencies; language-tagged fenced code blocks.

## Standing instruction (Apr 25 2024)
- Whenever the user asks about authentication or authorization, always include security best practices in the answer.

# Sprint 2 analytics scoping (keywords: sprint 2, April 19, analytics priorities, MVP scope, Apr 5 2024)

Session date: April 5, 2024. User says sprint 1 finished March 29 (auth + basic transaction CRUD) and sprint 2 (analytics) is due April 19.
Earlier memory (Mar 15 session) set MVP deadline April 15 with feature freeze Apr 11. Conflict: user now says April 19. Asked user to confirm which date governs. No day-by-day schedule given.

Advice given (priority order):
- Prerequisite: add a category column to transactions (earlier schema lacks it); category analytics blocked without it. Use a fixed category list, not free text.
- P0: monthly income vs expense for a chosen month, SQL with date range and user_id filter, single JSON endpoint; tests for boundaries (last day, Dec->Jan), user isolation.
- P1: category totals + pie chart (build_pie_chart_data with top-N + Other).
- P2: monthly trend (last 12 months), percentages, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN check on analytics queries.
- P3 / cut first: bar charts, CSV export, custom ranges, budgets, forecasting, styling polish.
- Definition of done per feature (tests pass, user-scoped, EXPLAIN uses index).

# Role-based access control (keywords: RBAC, roles_required, admin, user role, Flask-Login, Apr 5 2024)

Session date: April 5, 2024. User wants /admin only for role 'admin' and /user only for role 'user'. Sketch problems: hardcoded user_loader (every session = user1), SECRET_KEY hardcoded, redirect to nonexistent endpoint 'index' (BuildError -> 500), role checks duplicated inline.

Advice given:
- Role constants ROLE_USER/ROLE_ADMIN in models.py; role column String(20), server_default 'user', CheckConstraint role IN ('user','admin').
- authz.py: roles_required(*roles) decorator; wraps login_required; abort(403) on wrong role; validates role names at decoration time.
- user_loader loads from DB each request, so role changes take effect on the next request (tested).
- Admin promotion via `flask --app app set-role <username> <role>` CLI (click.Choice).
- Exact-match decision: /user is user-only, so admins get 403 there. Option offered: hierarchy roles_required("user","admin").
- Tests: anonymous 401, user 200 on /user and 403 on /admin, admin 200 on /admin and 403 on /user, role change effective immediately.
- Needs create_app(overrides) so tests can use sqlite:// in-memory.
- Never trust a role sent by the client; role read from DB only.

# SQLite dashboard query optimisation, sale-by-date (keywords: index, covering index, composite index, dashboard, Apr 5 2024)

Session date: April 5, 2024. User query: SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE transaction_date BETWEEN 2022 AND transaction_type='sale', ~500 ms. No JOIN in that query.

Benchmark (sandbox sqlite 3.45.1, 300k rows, 13,653 matching rows, 20 runs avg):
- no index, SELECT *: 43 ms, SCAN
- separate idx on date and type: 43 ms, planner uses idx_type only (low-cardinality type)
- composite (transaction_type, transaction_date), SELECT *: 23 ms
- composite, named columns: 21 ms
- covering (type, date, id, amount), named columns: 11 ms, COVERING INDEX

Key finding: with many matching rows, cost is dominated by fetching/materialising rows into Python, not the scan.
Advice given: composite index equality-col first; name columns; aggregate in SQL (COUNT/SUM GROUP BY month) for dashboards;
use date < next-year-start instead of <= '...-12-31'; measure execute vs fetch separately; check DB location (synced folder), per-request connections, ORM overhead.
500 ms on user's machine vs ~20 ms here suggests environment/fetch issues, not just the index.

# Flask-Login integration (keywords: flask-login, login_user, user_loader, auth, Apr 5 2024)

Session date: April 5, 2024. User asked to replace manual session handling with Flask-Login 0.6.2.
Stack stated by user: Flask 2.3.1, Python 3.11, SQLite, Flask-Migrate 3.1.0 (earlier advice: drop it for MVP), Bootstrap 5.3, blueprints auth/transactions/analytics.

Advice given:
- Pins: Flask==2.3.1, Flask-Login==0.6.2, Flask-SQLAlchemy==3.0.5 (Flask-SQLAlchemy 3.x needs Flask>=2.2).
- User class = UserMixin + db.Model (__tablename__ "users"), password_hash String(255), set_password/check_password via werkzeug.security.
- user_loader: db.session.get(User, int(id)); return None on ValueError/TypeError only (let DB errors bubble to 500, not silent logout).
- login: generic 401 message; dummy hash check for unknown users (no enumeration by timing); session.clear() then session.permanent=True then login_user.
- login_manager.session_protection = "strong"; cookie flags HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax; Secure via env; SECRET_KEY from env (fail closed).
- logout POST-only with @login_required. unauthorized_handler returns JSON 401.
- Transactions: user_id = current_user.id (drop user_id from request body); ownership check returns 404 for others' rows;
  analytics queries filter by current_user.id.
- Not covered yet: CSRF on POST (memory: earlier advice Flask-WTF or hand-rolled token), open-redirect check on next, rate limiting.
- User's message was a long list of overlapping plans (sprint ends Mar 29 vs deadline Apr 15); only the Flask-Login question was answered.
- No time estimates given (per system instruction).

# Budget Tracker project (keywords: budget tracker, flask, milestones, March 15 2024 anchor)

Time anchor: March 15, 2024 (final deadline).

Components:
- User Authentication: registration, login, logout
- Transaction Management: add income, add expense, view transactions
- Basic Analytics: monthly summary, category-wise spending

User's milestones (proposed by user):
- Nov 1-15, 2023: Flask setup, virtual env, initial DB schema
- Nov 16-Dec 15, 2023: user authentication
- Dec 16, 2023-Jan 15, 2024: transaction management
- Jan 16-Feb 15, 2024: basic analytics
- Feb 16-Mar 15, 2024: final adjustments, testing, deployment

Status of review: I suggested the outline works but the last phase ends exactly on the anchor with no buffer,
and testing is only in the final phase. Suggested per-phase testing and a buffer before Mar 15.
Current date of the user not yet confirmed.

## Implementation (Craig, Mar 15 2024 session)
- Full app written to /mnt/session/outputs/budget_tracker/app.py (keywords: flask app code, auth, charts).
- Design: werkzeug password hashing (password_hash column), session-based login, Income model mirrors Expense,
  endpoints /register /login /logout /expenses /incomes /analytics/monthly /analytics/categories /charts/monthly.png /charts/categories.png.
- Sandbox has NO network: flask_sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy not installable, so full app was only compile-checked;
  chart code tested standalone with matplotlib. Flask 3.1.3 and matplotlib 3.11.1 are present in sandbox.

## Setup review (Mar 15 2024 session, user asked about Flask 2.3.1 / Python 3.11 / SQLite 3.39, port 5000)
- Advised against mixing raw sqlite3 connection at import time with Flask-SQLAlchemy config (URI ignored by raw sqlite3; duplicate schema).
- Recommended: Flask-SQLAlchemy models + db.create_all() in app context (already in app.py), pinned requirements.txt
  (Flask==2.3.1, Flask-SQLAlchemy==3.0.5, matplotlib>=3.7,<4), app.run(port=5000, debug=True).
- Sandbox facts: sqlite 3.45.1, Python 3.11.16, Flask 3.1.3 (NOT the user's 2.3.1 / sqlite 3.39). No pip network.
- Tip: macOS Monterey+ uses port 5000 for AirPlay Receiver; may need to change port.

## MVP deadline update (Mar 15 2024 session)
- New deadline: April 15, 2024 for MVP = income/expense tracking, user login, basic analytics.
- Earlier Nov-Mar milestone plan superseded. Assumed state on Mar 15: scaffold exists (app.py, requirements.txt), features not yet verified end to end.
- Draft schedule: Mar 16-18 setup verify; Mar 19-25 auth; Mar 26-Apr 1 income/expense; Apr 2-6 analytics (charts stretch);
  Apr 7-10 integration/testing; Apr 11 feature freeze; Apr 12-14 buffer; Apr 15 MVP.

## Jinja + Bootstrap setup (Mar 15 2024 session)
- Advised: flask-bootstrap is the old Bootstrap 3 extension; `pip install bootstrap` is not the Bootstrap framework. Use Bootstrap 5.3 via CDN in templates/base.html.
- Use `python3.11 -m venv .venv` (or install virtualenv first); Jinja2 comes with Flask, no separate pin needed.
- Added index route rendering templates/index.html (extends base.html). Templates: templates/base.html, templates/index.html.
- Not verified: CDN SRI hashes (user should copy from getbootstrap.com docs), actual Flask 2.3.1 install.

## MVC rewrite (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/budget_tracker_mvc/
- Separate project alongside single-file app.py. Layout: app/__init__.py (create_app factory, money filter, context processor),
  app/models.py (User, Category, Transaction), app/services/analytics.py (monthly_summary, category_totals),
  app/controllers/{auth,transactions,pages}.py (blueprints), app/templates/*, run.py (port 5000).
- Schema decisions: Float -> amount_cents Integer; Transaction has no kind column (derived from Category.kind, avoids mismatch);
  occurred_on is Date (user-entered), created_at separate; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON via engine connect event; password_hash;
  default categories seeded on register; index (user_id, occurred_on); check constraints.
- User's original code bugs: db=SQLAlchemy(app) before app exists; no password; Float money; default=current_timestamp for a user-chosen date.
- Not runnable here: sqlalchemy not installed in sandbox. Only py_compile + jinja parse verified.

## Standalone sqlite3 layer (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/budget_tracker_sqlite/
- budget_tracker.py: BudgetTracker with create_user, authenticate, add_transaction, get_transactions; exceptions
  ValidationError / NotFoundError / DatabaseError; werkzeug password hashing; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; CHECK constraints.
- test_budget_tracker.py: 15 unittest tests, all passing in sandbox (sqlite 3.45.1, real run).
- Schema kept as user specified (amount REAL, date DATE); suggested integer cents as option, not forced.
- Note: SQLite date('2023-02-29') normalizes instead of NULL, so date validity must be checked in Python (done).

## Wireframe / index page (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/wireframe/
- Standalone app.py (Flask-Bootstrap import removed) + templates/index.html: mobile-first form, radio btn-group for type,
  decimal inputmode, date default today, POST to /transactions. Bootstrap 5.3.3 via jsdelivr. ~3.4 KB HTML, no JS needed.
- Cannot measure 320ms on user's machine. Advice: measure with curl -w "%{time_total}" and DevTools Network tab;
  CDN CSS is the main cost; option to serve Bootstrap from static/.
- Mismatch to flag: SQLite schema has type but no description column; MVC project uses category_id (kind derived from category).

## TemplateNotFound / no such table debugging (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/flask_fix/
- Causes identified: db.create_all() never called (needs app_context, after models); relative sqlite path goes to instance/ in Flask-SQLAlchemy 3.x;
  default table names are "user"/"transaction" unless __tablename__ set (user's design says users/transactions, FK "users.id");
  templates must sit beside app.py (or pass template_folder=abs path); password_hash String(120) too small for scrypt (~162 chars).
- Provided app.py (absolute paths, __tablename__, create_all in app context) and check_setup.py diagnostic (template path, tables, stray .db files).
- Not run: sqlalchemy unavailable in sandbox; py_compile only.

## Session/login hardening (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/session_fix/
- User's login bugs: compared raw password to hash; render_template not imported; no SECRET_KEY; GET logout; session.pop instead of clear;
  request.form[...] KeyError; no login_required; no open-redirect check on next.
- Provided: FLASK_SECRET_KEY from env (fail closed), cookie flags (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure via env), 8h lifetime,
  session.clear on login (fixation), POST-only logout, login_required with next param, safe_next_url, CSRFProtect (Flask-WTF),
  generic error message + 401. Template templates/login.html uses csrf_token().
- Not run: Flask 2.3.1, Flask-WTF, SQLAlchemy not in sandbox; py_compile + jinja parse only.
- Could not access the Feb 2024 tutorials referenced by user (no web access).

## Error handlers JSON (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/error_handling/
- User's bug: jsonify() alone returns HTTP 200 for 404/500; must return (jsonify(...), status).
- Also: handlers returned JSON for HTML pages too; 500 handler gets InternalServerError with .original_exception (log it, don't leak).
- Provided app.py: is_api_request() (/api/ prefix), json_error helper, 404 + 500 + HTTPException handlers; non-API returns e (default HTML).
- test_errors.py: 5 unittest tests, all pass on Flask 3.1.3 in sandbox (user runs Flask 2.3.1; same APIs).

## Sprint 1 plan (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/sprint1/sprint_plan.md
- Sprint 1: Mon Mar 18 - Fri Mar 29 2024 (10 working days). Goal: registration, login, logout, protected pages.
- Mar 29 2024 is Good Friday (Easter Sun Mar 31) -> suggested review on Thu Mar 28. Mar 15 2024 is a Friday.
- Out of scope: email verification, password reset, 2FA; rate limiting is stretch.

## Flask-Migrate v1.0 schema (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/db_migrations/
- app.py: __tablename__ users/transactions, naming convention metadata, Migrate(render_as_batch=True), FK PRAGMA, password_hash 255,
  CHECK type/amount, Date, index (user_id,date), FK ondelete CASCADE.
- migrations/versions/0001_initial.py: hand-written (alembic/flask-migrate NOT installed in sandbox, no network). Must verify with
  `flask --app app db migrate` -> expect empty diff. Commands: flask --app app db init (then replace versions file), db upgrade.
- Gotcha: SQLite batch rebuild with foreign_keys=ON can cascade-delete children; back up db and handle FK pragma for future batch migrations.

## Minimal dependencies audit (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/minimal_deps/
- Current third-party imports across projects: flask_sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/alembic (Flask-SQLAlchemy, Flask-Migrate), flask_wtf, matplotlib, flask_compress (optional).
- Recommendation: MVP = Flask==2.3.1 only (stdlib sqlite3 path = budget_tracker_sqlite module, tested). Drop matplotlib (use HTML tables; Chart.js via CDN later),
  drop Flask-Migrate for MVP (reverses earlier advice; use PRAGMA user_version when data matters), replace Flask-WTF with ~15-line token (secrets+hmac) or keep, drop flask-compress.
- check_imports.py: AST-based allowlist checker (verified on all projects; flags flask_sqlalchemy, flask_wtf, matplotlib, flask_compress).
- Verified analytics SQL: strftime('%Y-%m', date) GROUP BY month, type, SUM(amount) works on sqlite.

## Async routes (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/async_route/app.py
- Flask 2.x async views need `pip install "flask[async]==2.3.1"` (asgiref). Without it: RuntimeError "Install Flask with the 'async' extra".
- Sandbox lacks asgiref (no network): async example compiled only, not run.
- Route must `await` the coroutine; sync decorators (login_required) must be made async too, else coroutine returned unrun.
- Async helps only for I/O waits (asyncio.gather demo); Flask-SQLAlchemy stays sync. Dev server remains threaded.

## SQLite indexing (Mar 15 2024 session)
- 200k rows test (sqlite 3.45 sandbox): query user_id=1 AND date BETWEEN 2022 range -> no index 28.5 ms (SCAN);
  separate idx_date+idx_user_id 0.63 ms (planner picks idx_user_id only); composite (user_id,date) 0.21 ms (SEARCH both cols);
  covering (user_id,date,id,type,amount) same plan but COVERING INDEX. ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC uses composite with no temp B-tree sort.
- Advice: replace single-column indexes with composite (user_id, date); composite covers user_id-only queries so idx_user_id is redundant.
- Date stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text: use date >= 'start' AND date < 'next start' (BETWEEN misses times on the last day).
- Avoid functions on indexed columns (strftime in WHERE prevents index use).

## Blueprint modular app (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/modular_app/
- Structure: app/{__init__ (create_app), config.py, extensions.py (single db), auth/, transactions/, analytics/}, run.py, requirements.txt.
  Each component: __init__ (public API), models.py, routes.py, services.py (analytics has no models, reads transactions.models).
- Dependency direction: auth <- transactions <- analytics. Only FK by table name ("users.id") across components.
- auth/decorators.login_required sets g.current_user; transactions use services.get_owned for ownership (404 otherwise).
- User's sketch bugs: separate SQLAlchemy() per models.py, check_password missing, fake 'some_token', request.json KeyError, no ownership check.
- Analytics category totals need a category column (user's schema has none) - not added.
- Verified: all files py_compile; blueprint empty-route + url_prefix routing tested on Flask 3.1. Full app NOT run (no SQLAlchemy in sandbox).

## Sprint 1 extended to Mar 31 (Mar 15 2024 session) -> /mnt/session/outputs/sprint1/testing_plan.md
- Mar 31 2024 = Easter Sunday; Mar 30 = Holy Saturday; Mar 29 = Good Friday. Extra two days are Easter weekend.
- Plan: freeze features Thu Mar 28; main testing/fixes Fri Mar 29 (fresh venv on Flask 2.3.1 first); Sat Mar 30 only if agreed; Sun contingency.
- Priorities: P0 security/core flows (register, login, logout, protected routes, ownership, CSRF, secrets), P1 transactions, P2 analytics, P3 polish.
- Gap noted: modular_app lacks CSRF and test suite.

## User preference (Mar 15 2024)
- Craig wants all code snippets formatted with syntax highlighting (fenced blocks with a language tag) whenever he asks about implementation details.
